edbDesc: Fluids whose flow properties are not described by a single constant value of viscosity. In a non-Newtonian fluid, the relation between the shear stress and the strain rate is nonlinear, and can even be time-dependent. Therefore a constant coefficient of viscosity can not be defined. A ratio between shear stress and rate of strain (or shear-dependent viscosity) can be defined, this being more useful for fluids without time-dependent behavior.
title: Non-Newtonian Fluids
pickWhy: Umbrella term for several opposite behaviours; its listed uses (body armour) are shear thickening, whose card is in another batch, while shear thinning cases like thixotropy are their own entries.
